name: Adam Jarubas - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directive 2003/87/EC as regards revised benchmark values for the heat and fuel benchmarks for the period from 2026 to 2030
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to change how free pollution permits are handed out to industry under the EU Emissions Trading System. Factories get fewer free permits each year, and the Parliament wants to soften that cut for heat and fuel permits between 2026 and 2030. It also wants extra permits shared out: some to industry, some to the fund that helps poorer countries modernise energy, and some to the fund for clean technology. It asks for special benchmarks for some sectors, such as ceramics and glass.

- Extra free permits go to heat and fuel users, with some money going to modernisation and innovation funds.
- It affects heavy industry, district heating and factories in sectors like ceramics and glass.
- Parliament adopted its position; talks with EU governments come next before the law can pass.
